violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: salad mix in container on cold plate x 2 (55F, 52F) in serving lines (both sides).
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: CFM relocated both container of salad mix back to the walk-in cool back to 41F or below and served salad mix stored in walk in refrigerator.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: salad mix (47F, 49F), commercially prepared kimchi (54F, 47F) x 2 (both student serving line) on cold plate.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: CFM discarded kimchi and salad mix and replaced with back up from walk in refrigerator. EHS advised CFM to speak with management about removing white barrier with holes from in between the salad and kimchi container and cold plate.

violations.title: RTE TCS Commercially Processed Food, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is commercially processed is not used or discarded within 24 hours of when the original container was opened and is not observed to be date marked: marinara sauce in metal pan inside of walk in refrigerator with date marked label.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety commercially processed foods when opened and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of the original container was opened. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. This date cannot exceed any manufacturer determined 'use-by' date based on food safety. CDI: CFM placed date mark label on metal pan of marinara sauce with remaining hold date (6 days remaining).

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Observed on working chemical spray bottle not properly labeled with a common name.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. CDI: CFM placed label common chemical name (bleach) on spray bottle.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equipment/Utensils Air Drying
violations.observation: Observed multiple stacks of metal pans were found stacked while wet after cleaning and chemical sanitization on shelf near 3 vat sink.
violations.corrective_action: After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining before contact with food. EHS instructed CFM to allow metal pans to properly air dry before stacking.

violations.title: Cleaning Procedure
violations.observation: Observed a food employee rinsing hands with water only at the 3 compartment sink after digging in the trash can before returning to other tasks in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wash their hands and exposed portions of their arms by: 1) discarding used gloves; 2) rinsing under warm running water; 3) applying soap; 4) rubbing together for at least 10-15 seconds; 5) rinsing thoroughly under warm running water; and 6) drying with paper towels or air drying device. CDI: CFM trained staff on how to properly use warm water and hand soap for at least 20 seconds.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. Observed employees digging in trash can and rinsing hands with water only at the rinse basin at the 3 compartment sink before returning to other tasks in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. CDI: CFM trained staff on when, where, and how to properly wash hands.

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: Observed a food employee rinsing their hands with water only in the rinse basin of the 3 compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. CDI: CFM trained staff on washing hands at the hand sinks only.
